overview: The enterprise AI customer-support and agent market is undergoing a rapid consolidation and capability acceleration. Salesforce has emerged as the dominant incumbent player, with Agentforce achieving $1.5B ARR and integrated Fin (formerly Intercom) to own the full stack from agent orchestration to voice/chat delivery; simultaneously, OpenAI has launched Presence as a direct platform competitor, signalling frontier labs are moving downstream into enterprise deployment. The frontier model layer has fractured competitively—DeepSeek and Alibaba (Qwen) are releasing open-source models that match or exceed proprietary frontier capabilities at 5–20x lower cost, forcing agent platforms to optimize around model economics rather than pure capability. Despite this activity, market sentiment reveals a maturity gap: real deployed agents remain mostly chatbots, only ~25% of AI customer-service deployments deliver measurable ROI, and KeyBanc reports weak customer traction for Agentforce despite Salesforce's investment—suggesting enterprises are still learning how to operationalize agents profitably.

themes.name: Salesforce Agentforce Dominance & Consolidation
themes.description: Salesforce has scaled Agentforce to $1.5B ARR through aggressive acquisition (Fin for ~$3.6B), partnership bundling (Gemini, AWS, Siemens, Neo4j), and geographic expansion ($1B Switzerland commitment). Agentforce now spans voice, chat, coworker, and operations agents with pay-for-resolution pricing models. The product has achieved production deployments at Fortune 500 scale (Southwest, Live Nation, Adecco 27K users across 40 countries), validating enterprise appetite despite analyst questions about maturity.

themes.name: Frontier Model Cost Collapse & Open-Source Competition
themes.description: DeepSeek, Alibaba (Qwen), and Moonshot (Kimi) have released high-capability open-source models at 5–20x lower inference cost than OpenAI/Anthropic. DeepSeek is now valued at $52–74B with ~$500M ARR and planning an IPO; Qwen 3.8 claims near-frontier reasoning; Kimi K3 repeats the DeepSeek pattern. This has fractured the foundation-model market and forced agent platforms to optimize around cost-per-resolution rather than model capability alone. Samsung, Microsoft, and others are backing open-source via investment and partnership, creating durable competition to proprietary APIs.

themes.name: OpenAI Direct Enterprise Entry with Presence
themes.description: OpenAI launched Presence in July 2026, a managed enterprise platform for voice and chat agents with system access, managed policies, and built-in Codex-powered self-improvement. Early customers include BBVA, SoftBank, IAG; OpenAI's own support line achieves 75% resolution on Presence. This marks OpenAI's shift from model vendor to platform competitor, directly competing with Decagon, Salesforce, and Sierra in the enterprise agent deployment layer. Consulting-led deployment model (boots-on-the-ground pricing) mirrors strategy seen with PwC partnerships.

themes.name: Market Skepticism on Agent ROI & Maturity
themes.description: Despite vendor momentum, real-world adoption metrics reveal hesitation. Only ~25% of AI customer-service deployments deliver measurable ROI (Forethought); only 2% reach 'Center of Excellence' maturity (Forethought); KeyBanc reports 'weak customer traction' for Salesforce Agentforce despite $1.5B ARR; most deployed agents remain glorified chatbots rather than autonomous agents (Anthropic analysis); Spiceworks reports 'muted interest' from IT leaders for Agentforce; ServiceNow customers being pushed off SaaS to self-hosted due to agent compute constraints. This suggests a capability-marketing gap: vendors are positioning agents as autonomous workers, but enterprises struggle with production reliability, handoff logic, and justifying spend against head count savings.

themes.name: Product-Led Decagon Growth & Generative Analytics
themes.description: Decagon has crossed $100M ARR while deliberately rejecting the forward-deployed-engineer model competitors employ (a16z podcast, Newcomer). Recent product launches include Generative Analytics (conversation-to-insights), Campaign Composer (compliant outbound agents), Autopilot (self-improving agent governance), DuetBench-2 (self-improvement measurement), and GPU-efficient inference optimizations. The company is expanding geographically (Benelux, Brazil) and distributionally (AWS Marketplace). Decagon positions itself against the 'ChatGPT for support' narrative by emphasizing production-grade governance, multimodal voice, and business outcome alignment over raw capability. Customer wins span high-profile names (Duolingo, Away, Faire, Notion) with public case studies demonstrating retention and deflection metrics.

themes.name: Emerging Niche & Vertical-Specific Agents
themes.description: Sierra has positioned long-horizon Horizon agents for multi-turn customer interactions over days/weeks with outcome-based pricing (pay-for-results). Parloa has secured SAP endorsement and deployed voice AI at scale in healthcare, utilities, and retail (OBI: 89% CSAT). Cresta partners with Firstsource to address enterprise contact-center deployment gaps. ElevenLabs hired OpenAI's Enterprise Chief as CRO and expanded into South Korea and India with voice AI infrastructure. Ada's AI agent platform targets regulated verticals like loan servicing. These platforms are competing not on general-purpose capability but on vertical expertise, compliance, and operational integration—reflecting market maturation toward domain-specific solutions.

themes.name: Model Context Protocol & Multi-Agent Orchestration
themes.description: Sierra's MCP Gateway and Neo4j integration with Agentforce signal emerging infrastructure for multi-agent systems. Relevance AI released Omni (open-source self-hosted workplace agent) and Telem (search-quality routing across providers). Parloa's Forward Deployed Engineering translates customer needs into core-platform features. This reflects a shift from monolithic agent platforms to modular orchestration layers where agents coordinate across multiple LLMs, knowledge bases, and specialized tools. The market is moving toward agent-as-a-service scaffolding (MCP, RAG pipelines, tool registries) rather than plug-and-play agents.

convergence: Platform consolidation is fracturing along two axes: (1) **Incumbent CRM/SaaS vendors (Salesforce, ServiceNow) are bolting AI agents onto their existing customer bases and gaining distribution at scale, but facing maturity and adoption skepticism.** (2) **Frontier labs (OpenAI via Presence, Anthropic) are moving downstream into consulting-led platform deployment, charging boots-on-the-ground fees and competing on brand and model capability.** (3) **Specialized pure-play agent platforms (Decagon, Sierra, Parloa) are differentiating on operational maturity, vertical expertise, and outcome-based pricing rather than raw LLM capability.** The real collision is in the **model layer**: open-source competitors (DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral) have commoditized frontier capability at 5–20x lower cost, forcing all agent platforms to optimize around inference economics, prompt caching, and fine-tuning rather than proprietary model access. The pricing models are also converging toward outcome- or resolution-based billing (Salesforce Help Agent, Sierra Horizon) as enterprises demand proof of ROI before scaling spend. **Voice agents are becoming a standard feature** across all platforms (Salesforce Voice, OpenAI Realtime, ElevenLabs expansion), making voice vs. chat differentiation less relevant and shifting competition to latency, naturalness, and compliance—areas where task-specific optimization matters more than general model size.

predictions.claim: Decagon will reach $200M+ ARR by end of 2027 by capturing mid-market SaaS and B2C customer-support budgets that Salesforce misses or over-prices; Salesforce Agentforce adoption will plateau as implementation complexity and agent governance challenges frustrate enterprise deployments.
predictions.rationale: Decagon's product-led growth model, geographic expansion, and focus on measurable outcomes (Generative Analytics, Autopilot) align with market demand for production-ready agents. Salesforce's high friction (incumbent IT sell-in, platform integration, custom Koa training) and KeyBanc's 'weak customer traction' signal structural limits; Decagon's $100M ARR baseline and customer cohort (Notion, Faire, Duolingo) suggest runway to 2x within 12–18 months.

predictions.claim: OpenAI Presence will capture 10–15% of Fortune 500 customer-support deployments within 18 months by combining low activation energy (managed platform) with OpenAI model advantage, but will struggle to scale beyond enterprise consulting engagements due to high CAC and limited vertical depth.
predictions.rationale: Presence's early wins (BBVA, SoftBank, IAG) and 75% internal resolution rate suggest real product-market fit, but consulting-led deployment doesn't scale without building partner channels or product simplification. OpenAI's track record of platform commoditization (ChatGPT, APIs) works against premium pricing. Decagon, Sierra, and Salesforce will defend with operational maturity arguments.

predictions.claim: By end of 2027, agent platforms' primary competitive moat will shift from LLM access to operational maturity (governance, safety, cost-per-resolution) and vertical specialization; commodity open-source models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral) will power 40%+ of enterprise agent deployments as enterprises optimize for inference cost over proprietary model lock-in.
predictions.rationale: DeepSeek's $500M ARR, Qwen 3.8's claimed near-frontier performance, and Microsoft-Mistral partnership demonstrate durable open-source competition. Decagon's a16z statement that 90% of their platform runs on fine-tuned open models validates the trend. Cost compression is forcing every vendor to support multi-model routing. Inference economics will dominate LLM selection over brand.

predictions.claim: Outcome-based pricing (pay-for-resolution, success fees) will become the standard commercial model for enterprise agent platforms by 2028, displacing token-based and seat-based licensing as customers demand proof of business impact before committing to agent spend.
predictions.rationale: Salesforce Help Agent, Sierra Horizon, and payload-based pricing in OpenAI Presence all signal this shift. However, adoption will be limited by measurement challenges (defining 'resolution', isolating agent impact from human effort, compliance complexity in regulated verticals). Incumbents will resist; pure-plays will lead.
